subject: Finova decision criteria: SLA/latency/cost clarifying follow-up
message_1_subject: Finova decision criteria: SLA/latency/cost clarifying follow-up
message_1_body:
Thanks again for taking the call earlier today — great to meet the Finova team.

Recap of what we covered and a few follow-ups so we can align internally: 

Key decision criteria you mentioned:
- Latency targets: p95 inference latency target, 200–300ms for short prompts; some heavy batch jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- Cost sensitivity: target is to keep per-100k-token cost under a threshold you defined in the call (you mentioned this is a gating metric for final approval).
- Deployment mode: preference for private/VPC with customer-managed networking and dedicated capacity for production.
- SLA: business-critical availability and an SLA in the 99.9%+ range were discussed; procurement needs specifics (SLA uptime, incident response times, and credits).

Action items we have from the call:
1) Finova to confirm the exact p95 latency target for the primary inference path (short text generation) and any non-functional buckets (batch, embeddings).
2) Finova to confirm expected peak QPS and average prompt length so we can size Dedicated capacity and estimate cost.
3) Finova procurement/security to share SOC 2 attestation and any additional questionnaire items — we can map those to our Private offering controls.
4) Redwood to send SLA options and cost/throughput tradeoffs (attached: redwood-sla-options.pdf).
5) Schedule follow-up technical session with your infra/security and our platform engineers to validate network/topology and KMS requirements.

Quick question on economic buyer/timeline: who on the Finova side will sign the order form (title/team), and what is your target decision window? Knowing this helps us prepare procurement paperwork and any contract concessions.

I've attached the SLA options and a short checklist we use when sizing Dedicated/VPC deployments. Marcus is looped for pricing/commit discussion.

Thanks — available for a quick follow-up Wednesday morning PT or Thursday afternoon PT.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0148
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood-sla-options.pdf (summary of SLA tiers and credits)
message_2_subject: Re: Finova decision criteria: SLA/latency/cost clarifying follow-up
message_2_body:
Thanks Marissa — super helpful recap and the SLA packet looks good at a glance. A few clarifications from our side: 

Latency and throughput:
- Primary use case (user-facing summarization): target p95 <= 300ms for 90% of traffic. We understand spikes may exceed that for longer prompts.
- Background batch scoring jobs: can accept p95 up to 3–5s and can be scheduled to off-peak.
- Peak QPS estimate: ~250 concurrent inference requests during peak. Average prompt length: ~120 tokens.

Deployment and security:
- Production must sit in our AWS account/VPC with customer-managed networking (VPC peering or PrivateLink). We want Dedicated capacity with reserved commit if numbers make sense.
- Procurement will require current SOC 2 report and an org-level security questionnaire. I'm attaching the questionnaire and our procurement checklist.

SLA / procurement timeline:
- We are aiming for a vendor decision by end of May (target contract signature first week of June).
- Economic buyer will be our VP of Engineering, Priya Natarajan — I copied procurement on the questionnaire, she will be the signer.

I've attached the questionnaire (finova-questionnaire-responses.xlsx) with a few initial answers and places we need Redwood to confirm.

Next steps: can you provision a short sizing estimate for Dedicated (cost per month for expected peak/avg) and confirm the SLA tier that maps to 99.9% uptime and a 2-hour P1 response window? Also please propose 2 times for the technical follow-up next week with your infra/security engineers.

— John
John Stevens | Head of ML Platform, Finova
john.stevens@finova.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachment stubs: finova-questionnaire-responses.xlsx
message_3_subject: Re: Finova decision criteria: SLA/latency/cost clarifying follow-up
message_3_body:
Appreciate the quick responses, John. A few notes from Redwood pricing/ops perspective: 

1) We can size a Dedicated pool for the 250 concurrent QPS target with the 120-token average — I'll run a run-rate estimate and a reserved vs. burst model and share numbers in a pricing deck. Expect a draft by EOD Monday.
2) The SLA tier with 99.9% uptime and a 2-hour P1 response maps to our ‘Standard Enterprise SLA’ — details are in the PDF Marissa attached; we can confirm contract language for incident credits.
3) For Private/VPC hosting we support both AWS PrivateLink and VPC Peering; our infra team will need to validate subnet ranges and KMS integration.

Can you confirm the name/email for your procurement lead (Priya) so we can loop legal/finance with an initial SOW/Order Form template? Also, do you have a standard redline process (word/PDF) or do you prefer we start from our MSA and take comments?

I'll propose two tech-session slots for next week: Tuesday 10:00–11:00 PT or Thursday 13:00–14:00 PT. Marissa — want me to include platform eng (Soojing Lee) and infra (Ethan Park) on that invite?
message_4_subject: Re: Finova decision criteria: SLA/latency/cost clarifying follow-up
message_4_body:
Thanks Marcus — that plan works. 

Procurement lead details: Priya Natarajan (VP Engineering) — priya.natarajan@finova.com. She will own contract review and signature. Procurement prefers we start from Redwood’s MSA and provide redlines in tracked Word.

Tech session: Thursday 13:00–14:00 PT works for our infra/security team — please send calendar invite and include Soojin Lee and Ethan Park from Redwood. We'll have our infra lead (Sana) and procurement on the call as well.

Final quick clarifications before the tech session:
- Confirm Redwood's typical RTO for incident escalations and whether you provide scheduled maintenance windows with notice.
- Any special SLAs around data residency or audit logging for Private deployments?

If you can include a short SOW/order-of-magnitude cost attachment in the invite, that would help Priya and procurement when they join. Looking forward to Thursday.

— John
